Dear Petrolheads, Get Ready for the First-Ever BMW M3 Electric – Rendering
9 photos
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii
BMW is up to no good these days, as while the Neue Klasse design language keeps getting criticized, the company does not care about it. The Neue Klasse models have a face only a mother could love, save for a few exceptions, of course, and their cockpits, which look pretty much the same for what it’s worth, probably won’t age that well.
Thus, if you were dreaming to change your G2X, F3X, or E9X 3er, or perhaps an even older one with the new G50 a few years from now, when the depreciation will hit it like a train on the used car market, then chances are you will probably look for something else. Or would you? Guess only time will tell if the G5X is indeed an upgrade or a downgrade over some of its predecessors.
Mind you, the Neue Klasse design language is definitely here to stay, and it will also be applied to the upcoming BMW M3 . The premium compact sports sedan (and Touring) is gearing up to take an inevitable swing at the Mercedes-AMG C 63 and Audi RS 5, and it is in the making as we speak. It will follow the same recipe, as it will be visually more aggressive than the new-gen 3er, while also featuring a dedicated chassis setup, uprated brakes, a few changes on the inside, and more power than the M350.
The latter is the current range-topping member of the new-gen BMW 3 Series family, and has 437 horsepower to play with. The output equals 443 metric horsepower and 325 kilowatts, as that is how much is 3.0-liter twin-turbo straight six with 48V mild-hybrid assistance develops. The mill produces 428 pound-feet (580 Nm) of torque, and enables 0-60 mph (97 kph) in just 4.1 seconds, and that is the same as the 2027 M3 Sedan (base model), which has 473 hp (480 ps/353 kW).
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii We have yet to find out how punchy the all-new BMW M3 will be, but word on the street is that it might come with over 600 horsepower. The mill of choice will likely be the familiar 3.0-liter straight-six with dual turbos, which should also get mild-hybrid assistance. The upcoming M3 is understood to show its face in an official environment, with no camouflage on its body, sometime in 2028, perhaps touching down in USA for the 2029 model year.
In 2027, the company is expected to launch the first-ever BMW M3 Electric. Yes, you read that right, an all-quiet alternative to the ICE-powered M3 is being developed as we speak. And while it will utilize the iconic M3 moniker, it won’t share its nuts and bolts with its gas-powered sibling, nor with the regular 3 Series models. That’s because it will be the range-topping version of the new i3 Sedan, so it will utilize the same Neue Klasse NAx platform.
The model will feature a dedicated chassis setup, too, as well as beefier brakes to keep the extra oomph in check. Expect a few sporty changes on the inside, as well, and the exterior will be inspired by the M Concept Neue Klasse. The study premiered earlier in 2026, and has so far been used on most renderings trying to decipher what lies beneath the fake skin (camouflage).
The same goes for the model imagined by @avarvarii recently and shared in the gallery, which features familiar front and rear bumper, and a vented front hood, among other things. These were inspired by the show car mentioned above. This rendered BMW M3 Electric definitely looks a lot more aggressive than the new i3 Sedan on which it was based. It’s presented in yellow in this case, has some M logos, and a set of retro-inspired wheels, from what we can tell.
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii Depending on whom you ask, you’d get different answers when it comes to how punchy this model will be. Some believe it might have in the region of 700 (metric) horsepower in total, whereas others would try to convince you that a four-digit (metric) output is possible. We think that some 700 to 800 ps sounds more realistic.
BMW’s first-ever M3 Electric will feature a quad-motor setup with all-wheel drive, and will also have the 800-volt technology for quicker charging times. It will take an inevitable swing at the Mercedes-AMG C-Class, which is believed to have some 800 hp available via the right pedal.
As we already told you, the BMW M3 Electric is expected to launch sometime in 2027, whereas its ICE-powered sibling based on an updated version of the CLAR platform should follow it the next year.
Now, is the zero-emission M3 something that you look forward to? What’s your take on the design as imagined by the quoted artist? Would you ever see yourself driving one of these?
